doc.title: Nat Hentoff interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Joe Williams's 'survivors' remark and goodbyes
summary: Hentoff recalls Joe Williams calling them survivors, and the two thank each other to close.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Yeah. That’s for sure. Well I’m very appreciative of you giving me your time today.

Oh look, as you can tell I enjoy talking. But one of your friends, I was once in Joe Williams’ dressing room and we were talking about players who are no longer here, some because of their own damn fault. And Joe looked at me and said, “you and I are survivors.” And I felt like I’d been knighted, that Joe would put me in his company.
Well you deserve to be there, and I appreciate your time and everything you’ve been doing and are still doing. © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-
Well I’m glad you’re chronicling this because if we have a future — since the nuclear proliferation is now proliferating — but if we have a future what you’ve done is going to be terribly important.
Thanks a lot, I appreciate it.
